newsitem.title: UK: UK inflation falls to 2.7 percent in February.
newsitem.headline: UK inflation falls to 2.7 percent in February.

text.p: Britain's inflation rate fell to 2.7 percent in February, from 2.8 in January, after retail prices rose 0.4 percent in the month, official data showed on Thursday.

The underlying rate fell to 2.9 percent in February from 3.1, bringing it closer to the government's 2.5 percent target. The data contained good news for the ruling Conservatives ahead of the May 1 election.
The figures were below analysts' expectations and were seen as taking some of the pressure off finance minister Kenneth Clarke to raise interest rates, currently 6.0 percent.
Government bonds rose slightly after the figures.

"If anything the numbers are slightly better than the market was looking for," said Peter Osler, economist at GNI. "They will take some of the heat off the Chancellor (of the Exchequer) after the very strong figures we saw yesterday."
Strong earnings growth and a sharp fall in unemployment revealed in figures on Wednesday led to concern the economy was overheating and an interest rate rise might be needed soon.
